extraction.name: WebWalker: Benchmarking LLMs in Web Traversal
extraction.description: WebWalkerQA is a benchmark designed to assess the ability of LLMs to perform web traversal, evaluating their capacity to traverse a website’s subpages to extract high-quality data systematically. It focuses on text-based reasoning abilities using a Question-Answer format for complex, multi-step web interactions on a given root website. The benchmark is composed of 680 queries from four real-world scenarios across over 1373 webpages, encompassing conference, organization, education, and game domains. It is a bilingual dataset including both Chinese (60.5%) and English (39.5%).
extraction.creator: Jialong Wu, Wenbiao Yin, Yong Jiang, Zhenglin Wang, Zekun Xi, Runnan Fang, Linhai Zhang, Yulan He, Deyu Zhou, Pengjun Xie, Fei Huang
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The data collection process employs a two-stage funnel annotation strategy, combining LLM-based and human annotation. Root official websites across conference, organization, education, and game domains were collected. This involved mimicking human behavior by systematically clicking and collecting subpages accessible through sublinks on the root page. The root pages were initially identified through a Google search using keywords such as “conference official website” or “game official website,” followed by manual filtering. For the education domain, official websites of various university computer science departments were chosen. The dataset construction includes both multi-source and single-source types, corresponding to two types of human information-seeking behaviors within web pages.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Software Collection, Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator, Document analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Official websites, sub-links, and their respective pages, identified through Google searches and manual filtering. The content of these web pages, including markdown content and clickable HTML buttons, served as raw data.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: After LLM-based query construction, queries were verified and filtered for legitimacy, retaining only QA pairs with short answers containing entities. Web page content was processed to extract markdown content and clickable HTML buttons using Beautiful Soup. The ai4crawl tool was used to get web pages in a Markdown-like format.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: A two-stage funnel annotation strategy was used. In the first stage, GPT-4o performed initial annotations by constructing queries based on page information and specified roles (solo page or multiple pages). In the second stage, crowd-sourced human annotators conducted quality control and filtering to refine the final results. Human annotators rewrote and calibrated questions and answers to ensure QA pairs were correct and consistent. The process involved generating multi-step standalone queries requiring integration of information from at least two sublinks for multi-source QAs, and assessing if current knowledge from a specific document was required for single-source QAs.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: After LLM-based annotation, human annotators conducted quality control and filtering to refine the final results, rewriting and calibrating questions and answers to ensure correctness and consistency. GPT-4 was used as an evaluator to determine the correctness of responses by comparing predicted answers with ground truth using a CoT prompting strategy.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4o (for initial annotation and query generation), GPT-4 (for evaluation), Beautiful Soup (for extracting HTML button information), ai4crawl (for converting web pages to Markdown-like format).
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The WebWalkerQA dataset will be available at HuggingFace Datasets. The code of WebWalker will be released in GitHub.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset size is currently 680 high-quality QA pairs, with an additional 14k silver QA pairs not yet human-verified. The current approach only utilizes HTML-DOM to parse clickable buttons, lacking multimodal capabilities such as screenshots. WebWalkerQA is built on official websites with dynamically updated information, which means pre-trained models relying on static knowledge limited by a cutoff date may struggle to provide answers regarding web information published beyond that point.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The benchmark is designed to evaluate LLMs' ability to perform web traversal, specifically their capacity to handle queries embedded in complex, multi-step web interactions and systematically extract high-quality data. It is suitable for evaluating text-based reasoning abilities and problem-solving capabilities in web scenarios. The 14k silver QA pairs can serve as supplementary training data to enhance agent performance. It can also be used for agent tuning, involving fine-tuning models with golden trajectories to enable effective actions for information-seeking tasks. WebWalker can function independently as a web information retrieval assistant for a given webpage or seamlessly integrate with RAG systems to expand their scope.
